title: Console backlog decomposition + sprint 18 cut plan
content:
Context:
This doc is the working cut-plan for Sprint 18 (target dates 2026-06-08 -> 2026-06-19). Goal: lock a minimal viable scope for the console/tooling surface needed to ship the initial Dedicated rollout UI and the new routing policy editor, while deferring lower-value polish items. Use this as the canonical triage artifact for product, design, and eng sync on 2026-06-07.

High-level priorities for Sprint 18 (ranked):
1) Routing policy editor: core create/edit/save flow, validation, persistence, and feature flag gating (RED-2410).
2) Dedicated capacity onboarding: stepper + summary page for reserved capacity contracts (RED-2429).
3) KV/Prefix cache status widget: display hit/miss counts per model route (analytics surface for Optimize feature).
4) Console-API auth error UX: clearer error states and retry affordances for token/mgmt failures.

Sprint constraints and guardrails:
- Team capacity: 4 FE (console), 2 BE (api/ingest), 1 infra (deploy/test), 1 UX
- Hard cutoff: any item not in green by end of Sprint 18 goes to next groom cycle unless critical for Dedicated launch.
- Backwards-compatibility: changes to model routing API must be non-breaking; prefer adapter layer (RED-2501).

Scope decomposition (epic -> tickets -> rough points):
- Epic: Routing policy editor (RED-2410)
  - RED-2411: Editor shell + list of policies / skeleton (3)
  - RED-2412: Create policy form + validation rules (5)
  - RED-2413: Save/persist + API integration + optimistic UI (5)
  - RED-2414: Apply policy to route flows + rollback path (8)
  - RED-2415: E2E tests + e2e smoke (3)
  - UX notes: single-column editor with left nav, inline validation; wireframe v3 attached in Confluence.

- Epic: Dedicated capacity onboarding (RED-2429)
  - RED-2430: Onboarding stepper (2)
  - RED-2431: Contract summary + cost estimator widget (5)
  - RED-2432: Backend provisioning job (BE) + async status (8)
  - RED-2433: Error handling + retry button (2)
  - Wireframe: compact stepper to match enterprise flow; show reserved GPUs, region, SLA tier.

- Epic: KV/Prefix cache status widget (optimize)
  - RED-2440: Simple widget + API surface (3)
  - RED-2441: Metric chart + last 24h breakdown (5)
  - RED-2442: Low-cost UX: collapse to card on dashboards (2)

- Maintenance / quick wins
  - RED-2450: API auth error states (2)
  - RED-2451: Console telemetry tag for routing editor (1)
  - RED-2452: Accessibility sweep: dialog focus traps (3)

Prioritization rationale (how we picked must-have vs nice-to-have):
- Must-have: items that block Dedicated launch or cause incorrect customer state (routing editor save failures, provisioning jobs).
- High-value but deferrable: metrics widgets that improve visibility but don't break workflows (cache charts).
- Cutable: heavy polish, micro-interactions, multi-region UX copy localization, advanced filtering for policies.

Cut recommendations for Sprint 18 (what to drop if capacity tight):
- Cut: Policy tagging and saved filters (RED-2460) -> move to Sprint 19. Rationale: auxiliary; not required for creating/applying policies.
- Cut: Advanced cost estimator scenarios (multi-contract bundling) in contract summary -> keep basic estimator only.
- Cut: Full interactive mock in analytics (defer to Sprint 20)

Risk assessment & mitigations:
- Risk: Backend provisioning (RED-2432) could slip due to infra quota issues. Mitigation: provide mock async endpoint and wire up optimistic UI for FE to be tested independently.
- Risk: API schema changes for routing could cascade. Mitigation: use adapter layer and feature flag; add integration tests in RED-2415.
- Risk: E2E flakiness delaying shipping. Mitigation: mark only critical smoke flows as required for release and parallelize tests across infra engineer.

UX wireframe / acceptance notes (condensed):
- Routing editor: Left nav shows policies, center pane shows editor, top-right contextual help. Form fields: name, precedence, match conditions, target route(s), fallback behavior. Validation: no empty targets, precedence unique per project. Save success shows toast + link to applied route.
- Dedicated onboarding: Stepper steps: (1) Contract details, (2) Capacity config, (3) Billing & review, (4) Confirm + provision. Show estimated provisioning ETA after confirm.

Telemetry & rollout gates:
- Required telemetry events: policy_create, policy_update, policy_apply, onboarding_start, onboarding_complete, onboarding_error. Add console instrumentation keys to RED-2451.
- Gate for GA: 95% successful saves for 100 random attempts in staging, <5% critical errors in provisioning tests.

Open questions (to resolve on 2026-06-07 sync):
- Should policies support nested conditions in v1? (Recommendation: No, keep to flat match lists; add nested conditions as v2)
- Cost estimator: do we surface per-hour or per-month by default? (Ask finance; default to per-hour with month toggle)
- What SLA for on-prem customers? (TBD with sales ops)

Next steps & owners:
- 2026-06-07 design/eng sync -> finalize must-have list (owner: Ava Chen)
- RED-2411-2415 -> assign and spike on RED-2413 API contract (owner: Diego Morales)
- RED-2432 -> infra spike and mock endpoint if delayed (owner: Liam O'Neill)
- QA plan: smoke scripts for onboarding and policy apply (owner: Priya Kapoor)

Notes-to-self / rough timeline:
- Mon 06/08: start with RED-2411, RED-2430, RED-2440.
- Wed 06/10: mid-sprint triage to evaluate cuts.
- Fri 06/12: freeze scope for e2e and QA (only changes to fix-blockers allowed).

References & links:
- Wireframes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CON/Routing+Editor+Wireframes (v3 annotated)
- Jira: RED-2410 (routing editor epic), RED-2429 (dedicated onboarding epic)
- Slack thread: #console-rollouts (pinned message 2026-06-02)

Quick checklist for PRs to be accepted into this sprint (team checklist):
- Feature flag guarded behind "routing-editor-flag" or "dedicated-onboarding-flag"
- Unit tests for core logic + validation
- Basic accessibility checks (keyboard nav, focus)
- Telemetry events instrumented
- API contract documented in Confluence

If anything unexpected blocks core flows, call an emergency grooming session and move non-essential items to Sprint 19.
